title: fix(from-json-schema): drop redundant inclusive bound for draft-04 exclusive ranges
body:
## What

`fromJSONSchema` converts JSON Schema draft-04 boolean exclusive bounds correctly in *behaviour* but
emits a redundant, contradictory second check. For `{ type: "number", minimum: 5, exclusiveMinimum: true }`
the converter applied **both** `.min(5)` (inclusive, `>= 5`) **and** `.gt(5)` (exclusive, `> 5`), leaving
the resulting schema with two number-range checks where one is dominated by the other. Same for
`maximum` / `exclusiveMaximum: true`.

This change skips the inclusive `.min()` / `.max()` when the sibling exclusive flag is the boolean `true`,
so only the exclusive bound is emitted.

## Why

In draft-04, when `exclusiveMinimum` is the boolean `true`, the sibling `minimum` *becomes* the exclusive
bound — it is not an independent inclusive constraint. Emitting `.min()` as well produces a schema whose
internal check list carries a duplicate, weaker bound. Validation output is unaffected (the exclusive
check binds), so the duplication is invisible at the `.parse()` level and only shows up when inspecting
`schema._zod.def.checks` or round-tripping the schema — which is why it is easy to miss in review.

## Safety / blast radius

- Internal converter behaviour only; no public API, signature, or exported-type change.
- Behaviour-preserving for all valid inputs (the exclusive bound was already the binding constraint).
- The **draft-07 numeric form** (`{ minimum: 3, exclusiveMinimum: 5 }`, where the two are legitimately
  distinct independent bounds) is deliberately untouched — the guard only triggers on `=== true`.

## Testing

- Added `draft-04 boolean exclusive bounds do not emit a redundant inclusive bound` to
  `from-json-schema.test.ts`, asserting both the validation behaviour (boundaries rejected, interior
  accepted) and the structure (exactly `[greater_than 5 exclusive, less_than 10 exclusive]`).
- Full file suite green from repo root: **146/146 tests pass, 0 type errors** (`vitest run`).

reviews.body: > ✅ No new issues found. **Reviewed changes** — a tight, behavior-preserving fix to `fromJSONSchema` that drops the redundant inclusive bound the converter was emitting alongside the exclusive one for JSON Schema draft-04 boolean exclusive form. - **Guard draft-04 boolean exclusive on `minimum`/`maximum`** — in `from-json-schema.ts`, the inclusive `.min()`/`.max()` calls now skip when the sibling `exclusiveMinimum`/`exclusiveMaximum` is the boolean `true`. Strict `!== true` keeps draft-07 numeric form (`exclusiveMinimum: `) on the existing path as an independent bound. - **Add a structural test** — `draft-04 boolean exclusive bounds do not emit a redundant inclusive bound` asserts both validation behavior (boundaries rejected, interior accepted) and the internal `_zod.def.checks` shape so a regression that reintroduces the duplicate would fail loudly. The structural assertion is the load-bearing one; parse-level behavior was already correct pre-fix because `.gt()` dominates `.min()`. The `!== true` guard is the right shape: it covers draft-04 boolean `true` precisely without disturbing numeric draft-07 inputs, `undefined`, or the rare explicit `false`. Existing branches handling the numeric exclusive form and the boolean-to-exclusive promotion are untouched.   ｜ [View workflow run](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/actions/runs/26346798951/job/77557915351) ｜ Using `Claude Opus` ｜ [𝕏](https://x.com/pullfrogai)

comments.body:
Merging this. Pushed two commits on top.

The first pins the issue count. The check-list assertion covers the internal shape, but the thing a user actually sees is that an out-of-range value reported two issues instead of one — `expect(schema.safeParse(4).error!.issues).toHaveLength(1)` is what regresses if this is ever undone. Also dropped the `as any`: `JSONSchema` already types `exclusiveMinimum` as `number | boolean`, so the draft-04 literal type-checks unaided.

The second unstacks the comment, since `check:comments` landed after you cut this branch and fails on the pair.

One correction worth recording, because the squash message says otherwise than the description here: the duplication is not invisible at the `.parse()` level, and it does not show up in round-tripping. It is the reverse. `toJSONSchema` output is byte-identical with and without this fix on all four targets — `exclusiveMinimum >= (minimum ?? -Infinity)` in the processor makes the redundant bound invisible to the exporter — so no JSON Schema validator ever sees a difference. Zod's own parse output is the only place it surfaces. The bounds also aren't contradictory: `>=5` and `>5` are both true of every value that trips them, and the weaker one never fires alone.

Good investigation — the guard itself is right, and `!== true` is exactly the correct test to leave the draft-06+ numeric form alone. Thanks for looking into it 👍
